correctness.rationale: For the specified initial triple scalar periods coincide with triple returns. T^48=I mod 7; the triple fails to return at 16 or 24, covering the proper divisors of 48. If E=T^48-I, the first-order vector (E/7)v is (4,5,4) mod 7. Induction on seventh powers gives T^(48*7^a)=I+7^(a+1)B with B=E/7 mod 7, and a power coprime to 7 multiplies this leading term by a unit. This gives the least period at every level. For F_i(t)=P_(i+48t), the Mahler coefficient of binomial(t,j) is divisible by 7^j; converting to ordinary powers loses at most v_7(j!) and leaves coefficients tending to zero. After division by 7 the regular reductions are linear with nonzero slope; after division by 49 the three others have two simple roots each, since terms with j>=3 still vanish modulo 7. Hensel lifts give nine contributions of one and three of fourteen (two solutions mod 7^(k-2), seven representatives each mod 7^(k-1)); at k=2 the latter contribute seven each. The period densities and successive differences agree with every displayed mass. Independent replay python3 -B /workspace/checks/padovan.py computed the matrix columns by iterating the three coordinate seeds, recomputed the regular data and the exceptional roots (2,4), (4,6), (1,6), and directly stopped on the first triple return through k=6 (counts 12,30,51,51,51,51). The all-k conclusion uses lifting, not extrapolation.
